title: Fleet capacity + network quick checks (personal)
content:
Nightly personal checklist and notes — quick things I run through before signing off. Mostly shorthand, reminders, and follow-ups.

Context: dedicated fleet is seeing slightly higher mem pressure on p4d pools. Autoscaler_A hit burst yesterday; want to confirm routing and fallback rules are sane for weekend traffic. Touchpoints: SRE rotation handoff 08:30, Marco will iterate on spot-rebalance gate.

TODAY (2026-03-13) — quick log
- 07:05: look at capacity dashboard (console -> Dedicated -> Pools -> p4d-west)
  * current alloc: 62/72 GPUs (86%). baseline target: <= 80% for steady state
  * 5 nodes in pending provisioning (cloud provider lag)
  * mem pressure alert: 3 hosts > 78% GPU mem used (non-exec workloads from eval jobs)
- 07:12: ssh to mgmt jump (ssh aisha@mgmt1)
  commands I ran:
    kubectl -n rl get pods -o wide | grep p4d
    kubectl -n rl top nodes | sort -k3 -n -r | head -n 8
    nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv -i 0-3
  Observed: one pod (eval-runner-qa-3) pinned to gpu-2 on node gpu-05 and using ~22GB/40GB memory. Need to add a QoS evict rule for long-run evals.

QUICK TODOs (high-pri)
- [ ] Add eviction annotation to eval job templates: 
      resources.limits/gpu-memory: 28GB (approx) + annotation: "rl/infer-evictable: true"
      Reason: long-running evals blocking production inference during scale-ups.
- [ ] Update autoscaler_A config: reduce min_unneeded_delay from 5m -> 2m for p4d-west (test on staging first)
- [ ] File follow-up with SRE: confirm cloud provider retry settings for provisioning delays > 6m (ticket INFRA-2143)
- [ ] Run spot-balance script manually on staging (script: infra/scripts/spot-rebalance.sh) and capture output

NETWORKING CHECKS (fast)
- Check control plane connectivity to nodes in region: 
    curl -sS https://console.internal.redwood/api/healthz?region=us-west-2 (expect 200)
- Validate RTTs to cloud provider image store (S3 mirror): 
    ping -c 5 s3-mirror-usw2.redwood.internal -> want < 40ms
- Confirm BGP sessions on vrouter-gw-3: `show ip bgp summary` -> all sessions state: Established
- Reminder: recent change by network team (PR #542) added new egress ACL for ML buildpack images; might block older nodes. If provisioning fails with 403 on image pull, escalate to Marco.

CAPACITY NOTES / quick math
- Current steady reqs: 120 qps at 512 tokens average -> capacity plan suggests 68 p4d GPUs for 99th percentile latency SLO. We have 62 allocated + 5 provisioning = 67 -> borderline.
- If background evals kick in (x2 memory footprint), effective capacity drops ~10% -> need immediate mitigation (evict/cordon eval jobs)
- Action: set a short-term soft-quota on eval namespace to 30% of pool when alloc > 80% (implement via KPI autoscaling policy placeholder: /ops/policies/eval-soft-quota)

ONGOING INVESTIGATIONS (notes to self)
- Why did autoscaler_A pass on creating 3 nodes yesterday evening despite queue backlog? Logs point to cloud API rate-limit response 429 at 2026-03-12T23:18Z. Need to: 
    * correlate cloud provider metric: provider-api-errors us-west-2
    * add exponential backoff jitter in our provisioner (PR drafted, see GH PR 812)
- Memory leak suspicion in runtime v2.3.4? One host saw steady climb in GPU mem usage over 48h with same pod id. Steps: roll runtime to 2.3.5 on a single node in staging and run long-run evals.

HANDOFF ITEMS (for SRE on next shift)
- If alloc > 90% and provisioning pending > 3 -> cordon eval nodes and email oncall@redwood.com with subject: "urgent: p4d-west capacity high"
- If image pulls fail with 403 -> try node restart; if repeat, file infra-image-403 ticket and ping network team.

SHORT SCRIPTS / commands I keep using
- list hot nodes: kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.capacity.nvidia.com/gpu} {.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu}\n'
- top pods by gpu mem: for ns in rl eval production; do kubectl top pods -n $ns --containers | sort -k3 -n -r | head; done
- quick cordon: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force

OPEN QUESTIONS (write down so I don't forget)
- Should we deprioritize eval jobs automatically during transient pressure vs. always rely on canary fallback? Pros/cons to add to agenda for infra sync next Wed.
- How aggressive should soft-quotas be across Dedicated customers vs internal evals? Need input from product for SLA impact.

REMINDERS (personal)
- Merge PR 812 once Marco confirms backoff tests (blocking: unit tests failing on staging)
- Ping Owen about long-running evals schedule — ask him to add crude TTL on eval-runner jobs
- Update playbook: /runbooks/p4d_capacity.md with new cordon thresholds and eviction annotation examples (I put a draft section at bottom of runbook)

SNIPPETS (for runbook)
- Eviction annotation example: 
    metadata:
      annotations:
        rl/infer-evictable: "true"
    spec:
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/gpu-memory: "28Gi"

LOG (quick entries)
- 2026-03-12 23:20: observed provisioning lag; filed INFRA-2143 (assigned to Marco)
- 2026-03-13 07:15: cordoned node gpu-05 temporarily, drained eval pods, reclaimed 1 GPU slot

Notes to self: keep this doc minimal. Move finished items to a proper ticket or runbook. If anything urgent: call Marco (pager) or hit #infra-gpu.

-- Aisha
